tools.description:
Look up the tables, columns, values and measures a question is about. Call this first.

    Returns the Context Pack (what matched, ranked, with what was omitted) and a spec skeleton built
    from the best measure. Never guess a table, column or value name: ask here first. An empty pack
    with a `hint` means nothing matched, which is not an error.
    Example: find_data({"question": "credit limit by customer status"})

SpecSkeleton.description:
A starting spec, and what it was derived from.

``spec`` is deliberately incomplete: it is the table, the measure and the categorical column
that matched, so the agent edits rather than starts from nothing. It is ``None`` when no
measure matched, and ``note`` says what to do instead.

TimeMode.description:
The time intent. The agent says what it means; the server picks the column.

``events_in_range`` asks about a period (event time). ``new_since`` asks what is new since a
previous fetch (ingestion time, with a derived bound so late rows are not missed).
TimeMode.title: TimeMode

TimeSpec.description:
The time window intent, never a column (the server maps it: DESIGN section 6).

``events_in_range`` needs ``last`` (a trailing window from the execution time) **or** an
absolute ``from``/``to``. ``new_since`` needs ``since`` and is answered on the ingestion time
with a derived bound, so nothing is missed when a row arrives late.
TimeSpec.title: TimeSpec

    from the cached result, so a repeated call is cheap. Your own handles only; someone else's is
    reported exactly like one that expired.
    Example: get_more({"result_handle": "h_8f21", "offset": 100, "limit": 100})

tools.description:
Run one query spec and get a summary, a small sample and a handle. This is the main tool.

    Send `spec`, never SQL. The server lints it, prunes the partitions and the time window, picks
    the source, and answers with `summary`, `sample` and `result_handle` (page it with `get_more`).
    A `dry_run` in the spec stops after the plan; `fresh` skips the cache. Errors carry `code`,
    `problem` and an exact `fix`.
    Example: query({"spec": {"from": "billing.accounts", "select": ["customer_status"],
    "limit": 5}})
